title: Harmonices Mundi (Latin, 1619)
author: Johannes Kepler
description: Harmonices Mundi Libri V (The Harmony of the World), Johannes Kepler's Latin masterwork published at Linz in 1619. Kepler regarded it as his greatest achievement, and in it he seeks the divine harmonic order underlying geometry, music, astrology and the cosmos. Book I treats regular polygons and their constructibility; Book II the congruence of polygons and polyhedra, including the first systematic treatment of tilings and the discovery of two new star polyhedra; Book III the mathematical basis of musical consonance; Book IV the harmonic configurations of the heavens in astrology and the nature of the soul; and Book V the 'music of the spheres', where he relates the planets' extreme angular velocities to musical intervals and announces his third law of planetary motion (the squares of periods are proportional to the cubes of mean distances). It is the culmination of the Pythagorean-Platonic quest for cosmic harmony and a founding document of modern astronomy.
